- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward trends; increase forecast by 1–3% when true outcome shows rapid decline.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after high peaks, leading to premature troughs; delay downward adjustments by 1–2 periods.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust for lag by shifting forecast values forward by 1–2 days in subsequent periods.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., 88+ → 90+ forecast) — cap forecast at 10% below peak observed price in 3-period window.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <80) — increase forecast by 1–2% when true outcome is below 80.
- When true outcome is below 80, model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 1–3% for 3–5 days.
- Model overestimates in high-price regimes (e.g., >90) — apply downward bias of 1–2% for 3–5 days.
- Forecast mean is consistently 2–4% below true outcome in 30-day windows — adjust forecast mean upward by 2–4% for next period.
- Model fails to capture short-term reversals (e.g., 85→80→85) — add 1–2% upward bias after sharp drops to capture rebound.
